title: The Onward Brass Band lineup and Joe Oliver as ballhouse trumpeter
summary: He lists the band's drummers and members including his father and Oliver, and says Oliver played ballhouse style without a mute.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: You should hear those bands in those days, like the Olympia band, Superior band, and Imperial band, those was bands. And the parade, does he like the Armand Brass band? I mean, well, the Armand Brass band, I mean, they played my father, I mean, he can't tell you about that, because you didn't ask him about that. But I can tell you, they played ball house music. You can forget about what he said about the other fellas, you know, reading at that time. Yeah, but later on in the years, I mean, it was a Ball House band. Well, like you said, Danny Lewis on bass drum, well, they used them sometimes. But the main drummer that I seen played bass drum with the Armand Brass band was Bebe, or the, Jean-Vin and Bebe Matthews. He was two good drummers. And they played bass drum. No, he used to play a snare drum, but they, Bebe Matthews played. And Bill, Bill Matthews was a good drummer too, don't forget that. He was one of the top drummers you had too. He was in that category too. Well, they had, in that band, the Armand band, Bebe Matthews, Jean-Vin, they had Buddy Johnson on trombone. They had Vic Gasper on baritone, my daddy on alto. They had Manny Perez, Joe Oliver, and Kimball. Sometime they'd have Pete, Pete Bocas. But those three was the great guys. And did they play? Manuel Perez, Joe Oliver, and Kimball.
Who were the Ball House men in that band?

Who was the Ball House men in that band? Joe Oliver. He was the man. Joe Oliver, you know, he played, you know, like you have a third trumpet player on the end in the orchestra. Well, that's where Joe was in that band. But Manuel, I mean, he was just a, he made tunes, but you know, good tunes, but not like Joe. Joe was always, I mean, Joe was always like, you know, Ball House, like Lil Armstrong or Buddy Boll or something like that. You know, people like that.
He never used a mute in the orchestra. Who was that?
No, he never used, no, no mute.
They put their hands in front of the horns then? No, no, not in the street, no, no.
